rationale: The entry's core (lamp oil as Spirit-produced obedience/fruit stored and burned for visible light, not the Spirit Himself) is the best-supported reading of the supplied texts. Cross-references establish the lamp as the commandment (Prov 6:23), oil as received correction/truth written inwardly and kept (Ps 141:5; Prov 7:1-3; 23:23; 27:5-9; Ps 119:11; Jer 31:33; 1 John 2:4), and light as that obedience made visible (Matt 5:16). Exodus separates lamp oil (beaten olive for burning) from anointing oil; Zech 4 and Ezek 36:27 keep the Spirit as the empowering cause of the walk rather than the oil itself; the parable mechanics (finite store that must be acquired and kept beforehand, cannot be lent or purchased at the cry) fit proven obedience and refuse a direct Spirit identification. No rival accounts for the same inventory, purchase language, non-transferability, and lamp/light distinction with fewer stretches.
book_core_identification: Lamp oil is the tested fruit of the Spirit (inwardly received truth and correction worked into faithful obedience), not the Spirit Himself.
book_secondary_elaborations: stored as evidence of faithful obedience
burned to give a visible example that lights the Way
chapter_only_objections: Extended typological claims identifying the olive tree strictly as Israel and Gethsemane as the archetypal oil-press of Christ's obedience are chapter elaborations beyond the printed entry.
Detailed rejection of every ranked popular reading and the full fool/wise taxonomy are chapter applications, not entry assertions.
strongest_counter_interpretation: Lamp oil directly symbolizes the Holy Spirit (His indwelling presence, empowering, or illuminating grace), drawn from Zechariah 4, anointing texts, and popular readings of the ten virgins.
counter_core_identification: Lamp oil = the Holy Spirit Himself
material_core_denial: The oil is identical with the Spirit rather than the Spirit's pressed fruit (obedience) produced and stored in the believer.
counter_case: Zech 4 links oil-fed lamps to 'by my Spirit,' commonly taken as equating oil with the Spirit.
Anointing oil repeatedly accompanies the Spirit's coming (1 Sam 16:13; Acts 10:38; Isa 61:1).
Popular and some confessional readings of Matt 25 treat possession of oil as possession of the Spirit or His grace that keeps the lamp burning.
Sanctuary lamp oil (Ex 27:20) is read typologically as continual spiritual life supplied by the Spirit.
book_explanatory_advantages: Honors the explicit inventory separation of 'oil for the light' from 'spices for anointing oil' (Ex 25:6; 27:20 vs. 30:22-33).

Explains non-transferability, prior storage in one's own vessel, and the command to 'buy' (Matt 25:8-9; Prov 21:20; 23:23) without contradicting the free, non-finite gift of the Spirit (Acts 8:20; 10:44; John 3:34).
Unifies Prov 6:23 (lamp/light/reproofs) with Ps 141:5 (reproof as oil) and the inward writing of the law (Jer 31:33; Prov 7:1-3; Ps 119:11).
Keeps Zech 4 and Ezek 36:27 coherent: Spirit is the cause that produces the walk/fruit; oil is the resulting supply that burns as light (Matt 5:16).
Fits the wise/foolish distinction already defined as doers vs. hearers only.
counter_explanatory_advantages: Simple alignment with the broad biblical association of oil and Spirit via anointing.
Immediate devotional applicability to 'being filled' or 'keeping the Spirit's fire burning.'
decisive_sources: Ex 25:6; 27:20 (distinct lamp oil vs. anointing oil)
Prov 21:20; 23:23; Matt 25:3-9 (stored, non-lendable, purchasable oil of the wise)
Ezek 36:27; Gal 5:22 logic (Spirit causes the fruit/walk; fruit is not the Spirit)
Zech 4:6-14 (Spirit empowers the work; oil is the flowing supply; anointed ones identified, oil not equated to Spirit)
Matt 5:16; 1 John 2:4 (visible works/light vs. profession without kept commandments)
